# Find cluster markers

#### Find cluster markers of all clusters using wilcox.
```{r find cluster markers}

DefaultAssay(integrated) <- "RNA"
Idents(integrated) <- "integrated_snn_res.0.2"

cl_markers <- FindAllMarkers(integrated, only.pos = TRUE, min.pct = 0.25, logfc.threshold = log(1.2))
top2_cl_markers <- cl_markers %>% group_by(cluster) %>% slice_max(n = 2, order_by = avg_log2FC)
top5_cl_markers <- cl_markers %>% group_by(cluster) %>%  slice_max(n = 5, order_by = avg_log2FC)
top10_cl_markers <- cl_markers %>% group_by(cluster) %>%  slice_max(n = 10, order_by = avg_log2FC)
top50_cl_markers <- cl_markers %>% group_by(cluster) %>%  slice_max(n = 50, order_by = avg_log2FC)

top_cl_markers <- cl_markers %>%
    group_by(cluster) %>%
     arrange(desc(avg_log2FC), .by_group = TRUE)

write.csv(top_cl_markers, "Plots/Protocol_comparison/top_cl_markers_res.0.2.csv")
write.csv(top50_cl_markers, "Plots/Protocol_comparison/top50_cl_markers_res.0.2.csv")

```


#### Name clusters
```{r name clusters}

DefaultAssay(integrated) <- "RNA"
Idents(integrated) <- "integrated_snn_res.0.2"

integrated$celltype <- factor(setNames(c("homeostatic microglia", #
                                         "proliferating microglia", #
                                         "migrating microglia", # CHI3L1 (invasion, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6881255/), TIMP3 inhibits migration so maybe it is counteracting (https://www.nature.com/articles/onc201118), MT2A enahnces invasion and migration (https://cancerci.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12935-022-02623-w)
                                         "homeostatic microglia", #
                                         "activated microglia", # HLA-DR-genes
                                         "neutrophil", # neutrophil-like, FCGR3B-pos (CD16b) and CEACAM8-pos (CD66b) https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8773660/
                                         "mast cell", # mast-cell like, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8246912/ and https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5862545/ and https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-019-10291-0 ; ITGA2-neg (CD49b-neg) and KIT-pos (CD117-pos) in addition to other common to basophil and neutrophil markers such as CLC and GATA2
                                         "smooth muscle cell" # TFPI,IGFBP5, TPM2, KRT18, MT2A high
                                         ), levels(integrated@active.ident))[integrated@active.ident])
my_levels <- factor(c("proliferating microglia",
                      "migrating microglia",
                      "activated microglia",
                      "homeostatic microglia",
                      "mast cell",
                      "neutrophil", 
                      "smooth muscle cell"))

Idents(integrated) <- "celltype"
integrated$celltype <- factor(integrated$celltype, levels = my_levels)
ct <- c("proliferating microglia" = "#9A5C6B",
                      "migrating microglia"  = "#52788B",
                      "activated microglia" = "#4C8F69",
                      "homeostatic microglia" = "#ACA64D",
                      "mast cell" = "#E29C33",
                      "neutrophil" = "#DA7331", 
                      "smooth muscle cell" = "#DD4345")

pdf("Plots/Protocol_comparison/umap_by_celltype.pdf", width = 8, height = 4)
DimPlot(integrated, reduction = "umap", pt.size = 0.5, label=F, cols=ct) & NoAxes()
dev.off()

png("Plots/Protocol_comparison/umap_by_celltype.png",  width = 2800, height = 1800, res = 400)
DimPlot(integrated, reduction = "umap", pt.size = 0.5, label=F, cols=ct) & NoAxes()
dev.off()

```

# Gene ontology 
 
Gene ontology (http://www.geneontology.org/) provides a controlled vocabulary for describing biological processes (BP ontology), molecular functions (MF ontology) and cellular components (CC ontology)
Enrichment analysis provides one way of drawing conclusions about a set of differential expression results.

A useful link with information and example is: 
https://ucdavis-bioinformatics-training.github.io/2019_March_UCSF_mRNAseq_Workshop/differential_expression/enrichment.html

The steps here followe closely this demo:
https://ycl6.github.io/GO-Enrichment-Analysis-Demo/index.html

#### EnrichR
DE and EnrichR pathway visualization barplot generation.
```{r DE and EnrichR}

# DEenrichRPlot is a function by Seurat. 
# Default, which was used here, is to peform "wilcox" test between a group of cells and another group of cells. 
# Here I used some cell types against all other cells. Minimum p-values is 0.05 and the log fold change threshold I used is 0.3. 
# Different enrichR databases can be used (list here: https://maayanlab.cloud/Enrichr/#libraries) but I used only the Reactome 2022 for this analysis.

library(enrichR)

Idents(integrated) <- "celltype"

pdf("Plots/Protocol_comparison/reactome_2022_homeostatic_microglia.pdf",  width = 10, height = 5)
DEenrichRPlot(object = integrated, ident.1 = "homeostatic microglia", ident.2 = c("proliferating microglia", "migrating microglia", "activated microglia", "mast cell", "neutrophil", "smooth muscle cell"), enrich.database = "Reactome_2022", max.genes = 50, balanced = T, retunrn.gene.list = T, logfc.threshold = 0.3, cols = c("black"))
dev.off()

pdf("Plots/Protocol_comparison/reactome_2022_activated_microglia.pdf",  width = 10, height = 5)
DEenrichRPlot(object = integrated, ident.1 = "activated microglia", ident.2 = c("proliferating microglia", "migrating microglia", "homeostatic microglia", "mast cell", "neutrophil", "smooth muscle cell"), enrich.database = "Reactome_2022", max.genes = 50, balanced = T, logfc.threshold = 0.3)
dev.off()

pdf("Plots/Protocol_comparison/reactome_2022_migrating_microglia.pdf",  width = 10, height = 5)
DEenrichRPlot(object = integrated, ident.1 = "migrating microglia", ident.2 = c("proliferating microglia", "activated microglia", "homeostatic microglia", "mast cell", "neutrophil", "smooth muscle cell"), enrich.database = "Reactome_2022", max.genes = 50, balanced = T, logfc.threshold = 0.3)
dev.off()

```

# Cell cycle scoring

#### Perform cell cycle scoring
Load cell cycle genes.
```{r load cell cycle genes}

# Read in the expression matrix The first row is a header row, the first column is rownames
exp.mat <- read.table(file = "/home/marinani/PhD_Projects/Vascular_Organoids/Analysis/cell_cycle_regression/cell_cycle_vignette_files/nestorawa_forcellcycle_expressionMatrix.txt", header = TRUE,
  as.is = TRUE, row.names = 1)

# A list of cell cycle markers, from Tirosh et al, 2015, is loaded with Seurat.  We can
# segregate this list into markers of G2/M phase and markers of S phase
s.genes <- cc.genes$s.genes
g2m.genes <- cc.genes$g2m.genes

```

Cell cycle scoring.
```{r cell cycle scoring}

integrated <- CellCycleScoring(integrated, s.features = s.genes, g2m.features = g2m.genes, set.ident = TRUE)

# view cell cycle scores and phase assignments
head(integrated[[]])

# Visualize the distribution of cell cycle markers across phases
RidgePlot(integrated, features = c("PCNA", "TOP2A", "MCM6", "MKI67"), ncol = 2)

pdf("Plots/Protocol_comparison/umap_by_phase.pdf", width = 6, height = 4)
DimPlot(integrated, reduction = "umap", pt.size = 0.5, group.by = "Phase", cols = c("#bdbdbd", "#737373",  "#252525")) & NoAxes() 
dev.off()

```

Plot cell cycle scores.
```{r plot cell cycle scores}

# by cell type
# create a dataset
phases <- as.data.frame(table(integrated$celltype, integrated$Phase))
phases$Var1 <- factor(x = phases$Var1, levels = my_levels)
phases$Var2 <- factor(x = phases$Var2, levels = c( "G1", "S", "G2M"))

colnames(phases)[which(names(phases) == "Var1")] <- "Celltype"

# Stacked
pdf("Plots/Protocol_comparison/prop_cells_in_phase_per_celltype.pdf",  width = 10, height = 5)
```

# Comparison to primary microglia

## Compare to primary fetal microglai from Kracht et al. 2020

```{r load and prepare primary microglia Kracht}

## DE to primary fetal microglia
seurat_MG <- readRDS("/home/marinani/PhD_Projects/Microglia/Microglia_article/Objects/Co-culture_timecourse/Kracht_primary_microglia_seurat.rds")

```

```{r Seurat-based label transfer}

# Perform Seurat label transfer for projection of the reference onto the query (iPSC-dervied) microglia
# Find anchors
anchors <- FindTransferAnchors(reference = seurat_MG, query = integrated, dims = 1:50, npcs = 50, reduction = "rpca", k.filter = NA,verbose = F)
# Transfer the categorical information across the two datasets as predict.id
# Seurat does not correct or modify the query expression data
# Label transfer based on timepoint
predictions <- TransferData(anchorset = anchors, query = integrated, refdata = as.character(seurat_MG$timepoint_wks), dims = 1:50, weight.reduction = "pca") # project the PCA structure of the reference onto the query by default (this can be changed with the weight.reduction parameter). TransferData returns a matrix with predicted IDs and prediction scores, which we can add to the query metadata.
integrated$timepoint_wks_transfer <- predictions$predicted.id

# Label transfer based on cell type
predictions <- TransferData(anchorset = anchors, query = integrated, refdata = as.character(seurat_MG$celltype), dims = 1:50, weight.reduction = "pca")
integrated$celltype_transfer <- predictions$predicted.id

# Order metadata levels
levels_primary_wks <- factor(c(9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18))
seurat_MG$timepoint_wks <- factor(seurat_MG$timepoint_wks, levels = levels_primary_wks)
integrated$timepoint_wks_transfer <- factor(integrated$timepoint_wks_transfer, levels = levels_primary_wks)

# Plot the original primary data
pdf("Plots/Protocol_comparison/kracht_umap_by_week.pdf",  width = 6, height = 5)
DimPlot(seurat_MG, group.by="timepoint_wks", reduction="umap", pt.size = 0.6, cols = vintage_rich_cols(11)) & NoAxes()
dev.off()
png("Plots/Protocol_comparison/kracht_umap_by_week.png",  width = 2700, height = 2600, res = 500)
DimPlot(seurat_MG, group.by="timepoint_wks", reduction="umap", pt.size = 0.6, cols = vintage_rich_cols(11)) & NoAxes()
dev.off()

# Plot the label transfer by timepoint
pdf("Plots/Protocol_comparison/transfer_kracht_by_week.pdf",  width = 6, height = 5)
DimPlot(integrated, group.by="timepoint_wks_transfer", reduction="umap", pt.size = 0.6, cols = vintage_rich_cols(11)) & NoAxes()
dev.off()
png("Plots/Protocol_comparison/transfer_kracht_by_week.png",  width = 3200, height = 2600, res = 500)
DimPlot(integrated, group.by="timepoint_wks_transfer", reduction="umap", pt.size = 0.6, cols = vintage_rich_cols(11)) & NoAxes()
dev.off()


# Plot the label transfer by cell type
pdf("Plots/Protocol_comparison/transfer_kracht_by_celltype.pdf",  width = 8, height = 5)
DimPlot(integrated, group.by="celltype_transfer", reduction="umap", pt.size = 0.6, cols = col_primary_ct) & NoAxes()
dev.off()
png("Plots/Protocol_comparison/transfer_kracht_by_celltype.png",  width = 4100, height = 2600, res = 500)
DimPlot(integrated, group.by="celltype_transfer", reduction="umap", pt.size = 0.6, cols =  col_primary_ct) & NoAxes()
dev.off()

Idents(integrated) <- "celltype_transfer"
# susbet cells from each sample
hme <- WhichCells(integrated, idents = c("Homeostatic microglia (early)"))
hml <- WhichCells(integrated, idents = c("Homeostatic microglia (late)"))
am <- WhichCells(integrated, idents = c("Activated microglia"))
pm <- WhichCells(integrated, idents = c("Proliferating microglia"))
sm <- WhichCells(integrated, idents = c("SOX-medium microglia"))
mo <- WhichCells(integrated, idents = c("Monocyte"))
pem <- WhichCells(integrated, idents = c("Perivascular macrophage"))
er <- WhichCells(integrated, idents = c("Erythrocyte"))

# plot each sample separately
png("Plots/Protocol_comparison/umap_by_celltype_transfer.png", width = 5000, height = 2600, res = 400)
(DimPlot(integrated, cells.highlight = hml,  reduction="umap", cols.highlight = c("#9A5C6B"), cols = "lightgray", order = T) & NoAxes() & NoLegend() |
DimPlot(integrated, cells.highlight = hml,  reduction="umap", cols.highlight = c("#5F718B"), cols = "lightgray", order = T) & NoAxes() & NoLegend() |
```
